findings.title: STATUS wyrażony wyłącznie kolorem/tekstem bez chipa — brak rozpoznawalności w grayscale
findings.description: Status członka ('active') jest cienkim szarym/ciemnym tekstem bez kropki, ikony ani pilla. Per light-mode §8 status nigdy nie może być rozpoznawalny wyłącznie tekstem/kolorem — wymaga dodatkowego nośnika (chip/dot/ikona). W obecnej formie 'active' wygląda jak zwykła metadana, nie jak sygnał stanu. Naprawiane jednocześnie z migracją na StatusChip.
findings.canonRef: light-mode-readability.md §8 (differentiate without color alone) + §5
findings.suspectedLocus: AdminSettingsModule — Members & Roles table STATUS cell
findings.verifyNote:
Zrzut potwierdza realny stan: kolumna STATUS w tabeli Members & Roles renderuje status jako sam ciemny tekst (slate), bez chipa/pilla/kropki/ikony. To NIE jest stan loading (tabela w pełni wyrenderowana z danymi), NIE aging-color (tekst jest neutralnie ciemny, nie rose/amber/emerald), NIE link=primary (nieklikalna metadana). Dodatkowy realny defekt widoczny na zrzucie: niespójność wartości między wierszami — wiersz 1 'active' (lowercase), wiersz 2 'ACTIVE' (uppercase) — co potwierdza, że surowa wartość z DB jest wyrzucana bez warstwy normalizującej (StatusChip), zgodnie z opisem findingu o migracji na StatusChip.

KOREKTA POWODU (kanon-ref częściowo błędny): §8 zakazuje rozpoznawania statusu WYŁĄCZNIE KOLOREM i wymaga zdania testu grayscale. Tutaj status to literalny TEKST 'active', który §8 wymienia jako PREFEROWANY nośnik znaczenia ('tekst (preferowane dla badge statusu)') i który w grayscale pozostaje w pełni czytelny — więc rdzenny zakaz color-alone z §8 jest formalnie spełniony, a cytat 'rozpoznawalny wyłącznie tekstem/kolorem' jest nadinterpretacją (§8 nie zabrania tekstu samego w sobie). Realna podstawa findingu leży w sekcji §8 Implementacja (badge statusu = ikona+tekst+kolor+kształt) oraz §5/§6 (badge w tabeli — pełny zestaw tło+border+tekst), gdzie 'active' jako goły tekst nie ma afordancji badge'a i miesza się z metadanymi.

Werdykt: keep=true, bo defekt kosmetyczny/spójnościowy jest realny (brak StatusChip + niespójny casing). Severity P3 trafny — to polish/konsystencja, nie funkcjonalny blok ani problem dostępności (czytelność i grayscale są OK). Confidence: medium co do dokładnego paragrafu kanonu, high co do realności obserwacji wizualnej.

findings.description: Tabela członków ma nagłówki (MEMBER/EMAIL/ROLE/STATUS/ACTIONS) i akcje wierszowe, ale brak widocznych afordancji kanonu listy: brak ikony ustawień kolumn (Settings2), brak filtrów kolumnowych, brak sygnału preview pane (single-click → boczny podgląd). Per TABLE_AND_PREVIEW §1.1 panele listowe Admin są w-zakresie kanonu i powinny renderować się przez FilterableTable + TableWithPreviewLayout. Możliwy świadomy wyjątek (mała tabela inline) — stąd confidence medium; do potwierdzenia w kodzie.
findings.canonRef: TABLE_AND_PREVIEW_CANON §1.1 (Admin panele listowe w-zakresie) + §2 (SSOT komponenty) + §3.2 (Settings2)
findings.suspectedLocus: AdminSettingsModule — Members & Roles ręczna <table> zamiast FilterableTable
findings.verifyNote: Verified against source (src/components/Admin/AdminMembersRolesPanel.tsx) and the screenshot. Every factual claim is true: the Members & Roles table is a hand-written raw <table> (line 260), not rendered via FilterableTable or TableWithPreviewLayout (neither is imported); there is no Settings2 column-settings icon, no column filters, and no preview-pane wiring. Canon claim is also correct: TABLE_AND_PREVIEW_CANON §1.1 explicitly lists "Admin/SuperAdmin panele listowe" as IN scope (MUST apply canon), and §2 line 71 states "MUST: nowa tabela listowa = TableWithPreviewLayout + FilterableTable. Nie pisać nowego <table> od zera." This panel is an interactive list of org-scoped entities with select/role-change/remove row actions, so the §55 deciding rule puts it squarely in scope; the §1.2 out-of-scope carve-outs (read-only document tables, AI artifact renderers, cell/matrix editors) do not apply. No false-positive trap is in play: the finding makes no color claim (so aging-color/link-primary exemptions are irrelevant), the screenshot shows fully-rendered member rows (not a loading/empty/white screen), and there is no -ERR error-state context. Severity P3 is well-calibrated and left unchanged: it is a genuine canon deviation, but the table is functional with working row actions and only lacks the canonical list affordances on a small inline table — low user-facing impact. Note: unlike the Interview tables, §2.2 documents no sanctioned exception for this Admin panel, so the "possible conscious exception" hedge in the finding is not backed by canon, but it remains correctly logged at low severity rather than escalated.

Wg CANON §4.1 (honest UI — zakaz raw backend error jako jedyny komunikat) i TABLE_AND_PREVIEW_CANON §10 (Error = karta bledu + retry, nigdy bez wyjscia). Komunikat "global transport safeguard" jest niezrozumialy dla uzytkownika. UWAGA verify-before-claiming: plik nie ma sufiksu -ERR, wiec banner pojawia sie w stanie domyslnym; jednak moze byc env-specyficzny (lokalny backend blokuje requesty) — dlatego confidence medium dla samego fetcha, ale UI bledu (brak retry, raw text) jest realnym findingiem niezaleznie od srodowiska.

findings.suspectedLocus: src/components/Audits/* error banner (inline red text) — zamienic na kanoniczna karte bledu z retry + przyjazny komunikat; zdiagnozowac fetch/transport-safeguard
findings.verifyNote: Realny defekt, potwierdzony w kodzie. AuditsHub.tsx:419-423 renderuje surowy {error} = e.message w cienkim inline div (border-red-400/30 bg-red-400/5 text-red-600) bez ikony, bez karty błędu, bez retry. Komunikat "Requests blocked by global transport safeguard" pochodzi z client-side circuit breakera (src/services/api.ts:239) i jest niezrozumiały dla użytkownika. Łamie CANON §4.1 ("raw backend error jako jedyny komunikat" — zakazane, potwierdzone w docs/ui-standards/CANON.md:74) oraz TABLE_AND_PREVIEW_CANON §10 ("Error = karta błędu + retry; nigdy bez wyjścia", linia 458). To NIE aging-color, NIE link=primary, NIE empty-state — to faktyczny banner błędu z surowym tekstem. Defekt UI (raw e.message + brak retry) jest niezależny od środowiska, bo każdy błąd w tym module renderuje się tak samo. KOREKTA P1->P2: sam trigger (transport safeguard) jest specyficzny dla lokalnego backendu i rzadko wystąpi na prod; strona nie jest zepsuta — empty-state tabeli renderuje się normalnie poniżej bannera, jest workaround (re-load). To naruszenie honest-UI/polish, nie funkcjonalny bloker. Naprawa: mapować znane kody błędów na przyjazny tekst + dodać przycisk retry w kanonicznej karcie błędu.

findings.suspectedLocus: src/components/DocumentStudio/DocumentStudioView.tsx:227 (bg-slate-50) + DocumentStudioIntakeForm.tsx (brak owijajacej karty surface-default)
findings.verifyNote: Verified real, not a false positive. Code confirms the finding's facts: DocumentStudioView.tsx:227 sets the module background to bg-slate-50, and DocumentStudioIntakeForm.tsx:134-137 renders the form as `<form className="flex h-full ... gap-4 overflow-y-auto p-6">` directly on that background — no white card wrapper, no max-width constraint, no grouped sections; the only structure comes from input borders (inputs themselves are correctly border-slate-300 bg-white, as the finding acknowledges). Screenshot matches exactly: flat, lightly placeholder-feeling surface. Canon check confirms a genuine deviation: light-mode-readability.md §3 (lines 65-72) defines surface-app=bg-slate-100 and EXPLICITLY forbids bg-slate-50 ('nie bg-slate-50'), surface-default=bg-white for main containers, and requires every important container to have at least two means of separation — the operational intake screen effectively has one surface layer. Consistency check rules out house-style: the sibling PresentationStudioPage.tsx (same Deliverables family) uses the canonical pattern (mx-auto max-w-6xl main with rounded-xl border-slate-200 bg-white shadow-sm cards), so Document Studio's flat intake is the outlier, not a deliberate convention. None of the false-positive categories apply (no aging color, no link=primary, no loading/empty/error state). Severity P3 is correctly calibrated: text readability and function are fully preserved; this is a cosmetic surface-hierarchy/polish gap, which belongs in the lowest band. No adjustment.

Zrzut docs/qa/screens/documents/sheets-light.png pokazuje kolumnę OWNER renderującą surowy UUID (d2b6a316-08c5-47cf-9bf7-4ba5031...) łamany na 3 wiersze, identyczny w KAŻDYM rekordzie — nie nazwa, nie awatar, nie em-dash. Występuje na Presentations i Sheets, dark i light. Severity P1 trafny: nie blokuje funkcji, ale to bardzo widoczne naruszenie honest-UI na głównej powierzchni biblioteki, powtarzane w każdym wierszu, wystawiające wewnętrzne identyfikatory.

findings.title: Stan bledu bez widocznego przycisku Retry
findings.description: Karta 'Canonical artifact registry failed to load presentations' opisuje blad fetcha, ale nie pokazuje przycisku 'Try again'/Retry ani jasnej akcji wyjscia (jest tylko instrukcja tekstowa 'verify ... before retrying'). findings.suspectedLocus: Documents Presentations error state — brak akcji retry w komponencie bledu
findings.verifyNote: Realny defekt potwierdzony w kodzie. Blok renderu stanu błędu w PresentationsTabContent.tsx (linie 322-339) zawiera wyłącznie tekst: tytuł, komunikat błędu i podpowiedź ('...before retrying'). NIE ma żadnego przycisku Retry/Try again, ani innego elementu akcji (brak <button>, onClick, refetch/reload). Karta dosłownie pisze 'before retrying', ale nie daje kontrolki do ponowienia. To narusza TABLE_AND_PREVIEW_CANON §10 (linia 458: 'Error: karta błędu + retry; nigdy ... bez wyjścia') oraz DoD §10 (linia 936: 'Error = karta + retry'). NIE jest to fałszywy alarm: kolor karty jest amber/cream (miękkie ostrzeżenie, intencjonalny — NIE crimson-leak), więc zarzut nie dotyczy koloru lecz braku akcji retry. Sam fetch-błąd może być env-specyficzny (lokalny DB/scope, banner LOCAL widoczny), ale finding słusznie dotyczy UI stanu, nie samego fetcha. Severity P2 trafny: użytkownik nie jest całkowicie zablokowany (sidebar i inne zakładki nadal działają = wyjście na poziomie aplikacji istnieje), ale wewnątrz karty błędu nie ma odzysku — wymusza pełny reload/nawigację. To jawne naruszenie MUST kanonu na głównym stanie treści, ale bez utraty danych — nie P1, nie P3.

NIE jest to falszywy alarm z listy wyjatkow (brak aging-color, link=primary, loading, error-state). Widoczne realne defekty: (1) duplikaty tytulow — "Structured sheet draft" x3 oraz obciety "Utw" x2 (prawdopodobnie urwane "Utwórz..."), co potwierdza niska jakosc seed-data; (2) kolumna OWNER pokazuje surowy UUID (d2b6a316-08c5-47cf-9bf7-4ba50311d5a2) zamiast nazwy/osoby we WSZYSTKICH wierszach — to faktyczne naruszenie kanonu renderowania kolumn i uczciwych/czytelnych danych (TABLE_AND_PREVIEW_CANON §13, CANON §4.1). Korekta opisu: naglowek "cala tabela = placeholder o zerowej roznorodnosci" jest zawyzony — gorne 3 wiersze maja sensowne, rozne tytuly PL ("Stwórz: Tracker zadań...", "Wypisz ryzyka...", "Stwórz: Zestaw OKR..."). Uniformnosc kolumn TYP=Sheet/VISIBILITY=Organization/EXPORTS=XLSX/STATUS=Ready jest prawdopodobnie INTENCJONALNA (wszystkie to legalnie arkusze org/XLSX/gotowe) i sama w sobie nie jest defektem. Mimo to rdzen findingu (duplikaty + surowy UUID jako owner) jest prawdziwy. Severity P2 trafny — to kosmetyka/jakosc danych, nie blokada funkcjonalna. Confidence: medium (defekt potwierdzony wizualnie, ale headline wymaga korekty zakresu).

findings.title: DEADLINE + osobna kolumna ALERTS zamiast jednego modelu terminu (DueChip)
findings.description: Tabela Summary ma osobna kolumne DEADLINE (z czerwonym zegarem) ORAZ osobna kolumne ALERTS ('OK'). Kanon §4.4 wymaga JEDNEGO modelu terminu: jedna kolumna 'Termin' z DueChip (neutral/warning/danger), nie rozbicia na DEADLINE + osobny alarm-kolumne, ktore sobie przecza (deadline crimson vs alerts OK). Status chip 'Executing' jako info-blue dot jest zgodny z §4.1 (in_progress→info) — to PASS; finding dotyczy rozjazdu DEADLINE vs ALERTS jako dwoch kolumn sygnalu.
findings.canonRef: TABLE_AND_PREVIEW §4.4 (jeden DueChip, nie dwie kolumny sygnalu czasu/ryzyka)
findings.suspectedLocus: src/components/Execution/Summary — kolumny DEADLINE + ALERTS; rozwazyc konsolidacje do jednego DueChip
findings.verifyNote:
Zrzut potwierdza dwie osobne kolumny niosące sygnał czasu/ryzyka: DEADLINE (zegar + data, ikona w czerwieni) ORAZ ALERTS ("• OK"). Kanon §4.4 (linie 184-185) jest jednoznaczny: MUST = jedna kolumna "Termin" z DueChip (neutral/warning/danger niesione przez ikonę/kropkę, shell neutralny); MUST NOT = dwie osobne kolumny dla sygnału terminu. To realna dewiacja strukturalna od modelu jednego DueChip, nie intencjonalny design.

Sceptyczne kontrole NIE obalają findingu: (1) czerwony zegar NIE jest aging-color na dacie/wieku ani link=primary — to ikona w kolumnie DEADLINE, czyli właśnie miejsce, gdzie kanon dopuszcza czerwień TYLKO przez DueChip; (2) status chip "Executing" jako info-blue jest zgodny z §4.1 (PASS, zgodnie z opisem); (3) nie ma pustego ekranu/stanu loading. Dodatkowo daty (4/5/2026, 5/5/2026) są w przeszłości względem dziś (2026-06-17) i aktywny jest filtr "Missing Dates 6" — więc rozjazd jest namacalny: DEADLINE niesie sygnał danger (czerwony zegar), a ALERTS twierdzi "OK".

Niepewność (confidence: medium, nie high): kolumna ALERTS może w zamyśle agregować alerty SZERSZE niż sam termin (blocked / overdue decisions / missing dates — patrz chipy filtrów u góry). Jeśli ALERTS nie jest czystym lustrem due-state, ścisły zakaz §4.4 "dwie kolumny tego samego sygnału czasu" stosuje się słabiej — wciąż jednak pozostaje rozjazd danger-deadline vs OK-alert, który dezorientuje. Severity P3 trafny: to dewiacja strukturalno-kosmetyczna od kanonu, bez złamania funkcji. Do zamknięcia wymaga decyzji produktowej: albo zwinąć sygnał terminu do jednego DueChip, albo jawnie przedefiniować ALERTS jako kolumnę NIE-terminową (i wtedy dopilnować, by DEADLINE używał DueChip z danger dla overdue zamiast surowego czerwonego zegara).

The "AI Balance workload" element is NOT a sub-filter chip governed by §4.0a — it is a separate AI ACTION BUTTON rendered via the documented shared SSOT getMenu3AiButtonClass (src/components/Initiatives/Analysis/ResourcesAnalysis.tsx:541-548 -> src/components/shared/ModuleHub/menu3ActionButtonStyles.ts). Pixel-sampled the badges in inbox-light.png (2x crop): "Submitted" text = rgb(2,104,51) ~emerald-700/800 on near-white fill, contrast 6.86:1; "Assigned" text = rgb(60,41,132) ~indigo-700/800, contrast 11.28:1. findings.verifyNote: Verified real, not a false positive. Code path in src/components/Meeting/MeetingHub.tsx: on fetch failure the catch block sets setMeetings([]) (line 122) and setLoadError(...) (line 123). The filter chips are built from counts = useMemo over meetings.length (lines 220-229) and passed via commandRowContent into ModuleHub's persistent header (chips array lines 311-356). Two problems vs canon: (1) purple/violet is not part of the Consultify palette (primary=crimson, accent=navy, plus semantic info/success/warning/danger and the bounded tag palette c-tag-*) — CANON §1/§4.0a forbid a new local visual language and restrict identity colors to the stłumiona c-tag palette; (2) even ignoring hue, a fully color-saturated wall fails the §4.0 test ('if you see a lot of one strong color at once → misuse; the work surface must be calm, color only when it means something'). findings.verifyNote: REAL defect, verified in both light and dark screens. Every calendar event bar is a solid saturated violet-600 (#7c3aed) fill that dominates the canvas. Root cause traced to server: server/src/routes/my-work/calendar.routes.ts:366 and :442 hardcode initiative + milestone events to color:'#7c3aed', which CalendarGrid.tsx:84 applies as backgroundColor. The seed/demo data is initiative-heavy ("Cloud Migration Phase 2", "Cybersecurity Enhancement Program", "RPA implementation"), so the grid becomes a wall of violet. Ruled out all false-positive patterns: not aging-color (violet is not a fresh/warm/critical age tone), not link=primary (these are filled bars, not text links), not loading/empty, not an error-state screenshot. The violation is genuine against the module SSOT TIMELINE_CALENDAR_CANON.md (§2.4 normal chips = bg-slate-50 calm; §2.3/§2.2 use amber/rose semantics; §2.5 "Do not override bars with primary") and against the calm-worktool/color=signal principle (a fully saturated wall of one strong color = misuse). TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding's reasoning that should be noted: (1) the claim "violet is not part of the Consultify palette" is INACCURATE — #7c3aed/violet-600 IS the brand primary color in this codebase (color-system.md and GOLDEN both define primary as "primary/violet-blue" for selection/focus/CTA). The actual violation is using primary/violet as a saturated DECORATIVE FILL, which is explicitly forbidden (color-system.md:300 and :326, GOLDEN:440: "primary/violet is forbidden as decorative metadata chip fill"), plus overriding the source-coded SOURCE_COLORS identity (initiative should render crimson #A51C30 per calendarTypes.ts but the server color overrides it). (2) There is an internal inconsistency: client SOURCE_COLORS gives initiatives crimson, but the server color field wins and forces violet. Severity corrected P1->P2: this is a cosmetic/styling defect with no functional breakage (events readable, clickable, filterable); the canon violation + dominant-color + cross-theme scope justify keeping it as a real bug but not a P1.

findings.title: Decisions overdue DueChip rendered fully neutral grey — no danger signal
findings.description: Due Date chips reading '86d overdue', '80d overdue', '89d overdue', '85d overdue' are rendered with a neutral grey shell, slate clock icon and slate text — zero red/danger pixels measured in the column. Per TABLE_AND_PREVIEW_CANON §4.4 overdue MUST be the danger tone (AlertTriangle/red icon + 'Xd overdue'), and light-mode-readability §5/§18.2 require danger to read as danger in light. A months-overdue decision currently looks identical to an on-track date — the most important alarm in the table is invisible. This is the VIS-001 'danger loses fill in light' pattern applied to the due/overdue chip.
findings.canonRef: TABLE_AND_PREVIEW_CANON §4.4 (overdue = danger via icon/color); light-mode-readability §5, §8, §18.2 (badge danger MUST have fill in light)
findings.suspectedLocus: Decisions table DueChip/due-date cell — overdue branch not mapping to danger tone (DueChip in src/components/ui/primitives/chips, or a local decisions due renderer bypassing it)
findings.verifyNote: Verified against screenshot + source (src/components/MyWork/DecisionsPanelContent.tsx). The screenshot shows Approved/Escalated decisions whose Due Date chips read "86d/80d/89d/85d overdue" rendered fully neutral (grey shell, slate clock, slate text) — finding's visual claim is accurate. ROOT CAUSE: line 601 passes risk={overdue ? 'overdue' : 'none'} but `overdue` is gated on status==='PENDING' (line 414/676 isOverdue(dueDate) && status==='PENDING'), while the label string is computed independently by formatDate() (line 221: diffDays < -1 -> "Xd overdue") with NO status gate. So a past-due Approved/Escalated decision prints the WORD "overdue" while the tone is forced neutral. This is NOT the VIS-001 fill-loss pattern: DueChip.tsx correctly applies CHIP_TONE_VAR.danger to icon+text when risk==='overdue' — danger fill works fine, the component simply isn't asked for it. The real defect is narrower: label/tone DECOUPLING that technically violates canon §4.4 ("przekroczone = danger, ikona + 'Xd overdue'" ties the overdue wording to the danger tone). MITIGATION / why downgrade from P1: every visible row is Approved or Escalated (non-actionable / already-resolved), where suppressing a missed-deadline alarm is a defensible product decision (a made decision's deadline is moot; Escalated already carries its own amber status chip). No PENDING+overdue row is visible to prove an actionable alarm is being swallowed, so the finding's "most important alarm is invisible" framing is overstated. Genuine but low-impact polish/consistency bug, not a missing-alarm P1. Recommended fix: gate the "Xd overdue" wording (formatDate) on the same PENDING condition, OR apply danger whenever the label says overdue. Confidence: medium-high on the decoupling fact (code-verified); the severity call is the judgment.

findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED real defect, not a false positive. Tried to disprove it and could not. Screenshot + code + canon all align. Screenshot (docs/qa/screens/my-work/inbox-light.png, zoomed) shows the Inbox 'Critical' urgency badge as a white/transparent pill with neutral gray border and dark slate 'Critical' text, with only a small red AlertTriangle icon carrying the danger signal — no danger background, border, or text color. This is the INTENTIONAL aging signal (VIS-002 / §18.1), NOT a crimson/text-primary leak — the finding correctly states this and recommends no color-code change. The real, valid issue is demo-data staleness: today is 2026-06-17 but seed receivedAt dates are 2-3 months old, so every row saturates into the 'critical' bucket. Result is a wall of one alarm color where the fresh->emerald / warm->amber / critical->rose gradient carries no information and cannot be demonstrated (mild §4.0 concern). findings.title: Manager 'Team Capacity 512% utilized' — implausible metric value
findings.description: The Manager dashboard Team Capacity card shows '512% utilized'. A capacity-utilization metric over 100% (5x) reads as broken/unbelievable data rather than a real signal and undermines trust in the executive cockpit. Likely a seed/aggregation issue (sum of assignments vs available hours) rather than a styling bug, but it is the most visually jarring data point on the screen. Recommend clamping/validating the metric or fixing the demo data.
findings.canonRef: CANON §4.1 (honest UI — no implausible/NaN-like values presented as fact)
findings.suspectedLocus: Manager portfolio-health aggregation / demo data (team capacity calc)
findings.verifyNote: Real finding, not a false alarm. Verified the value is genuine unclamped arithmetic, not a styling/aging/loading artifact. Source chain: ExecutiveDashboard/KPIGrid render `kpiData.team.avgCapacity%` with subValue "utilized" (KPIGrid.tsx:335-338); avgCapacity is a plain mean of per-member `capacity` (ExecutiveDashboard.tsx:457-460) = `utilizationPercent` from /my-work/team-workload (stats.routes.ts:171) → getCapacityOverview (workloadCapacityService.ts:159): `util = round(alloc/cap*100)` with NO upper clamp. capacityHours is capped (allocation_percent clamped 0-100 ×40h, line 111) but allocatedHours = uncapped SUM(estimated_hours) over all open tasks (line 127), so a user overloaded with task estimates yields util far above 100%, and the FE average is likewise unclamped. 512% is therefore real seed/aggregation output, exactly as the finding diagnosed. It is NOT covered by any exception category (no date/aging-color, no link=primary, not loading/empty, not an -ERR error-state screen). CANON §4.1 honest-UI applies: a 5x value reads as broken data in an executive cockpit. Note the card DOES intentionally treat >100% as a meaningful overload signal (overloaded count, danger status), so a modest >100% is by-design; only the implausible magnitude (512%) and absence of any sanity clamp are the issue. Severity P3 is accurate: cosmetic/trust, single data point, demo-data-driven on a local org screenshot, no crash. Recommend clamping/validating avgCapacity display or fixing demo distribution.

findings.verifyNote: Real, deterministic defect confirmed by screenshot AND source/locale inspection. In src/components/settings/AIBehaviorSettings.tsx the field labels are rendered via t('settings.ai.tone'), t('settings.ai.formality'), t('settings.ai.verbosity') (lines 334/342/351). But in public/locales/en/translation.json (lines 4633-4649) those same keys are OBJECTS holding the dropdown option values (tone.professional, formality.formal, verbosity.minimal, etc.). i18next therefore returns the literal warning 'key ... (en) returned an object instead of string' and does NOT fall back to the provided default ('Tone'/'Formality'/'Verbosity'), since the key resolves to an object. Result is raw i18n error text shown as the only field label — a clear honest-UI violation (CANON §4.1) and unreadable domain label (§5 DoD). Fix = use distinct label keys (e.g. settings.ai.toneLabel) or read the object's children. 'Updates on tasks assigned to you', 'Weekly summary of activity') praktycznie znika, stopka 'All changes saved / Save Changes' wtopiona w ciemne tło. findings.suspectedLocus: Wspólny wrapper panelu Settings (np. SettingsPanelShell / SettingsSection) — prawdopodobnie pozostawiony `bg-black/40` lub `opacity`/`saving`-overlay nie zdejmowany po fetchu; sprawdzić komponenty paneli AI/Notifications/Security w src/components/Settings (lub views/settings). Możliwy też wspólny LoadingOverlay z is-loading stuck.
findings.verifyNote: REAL defect, confirmed by screenshot + code. Tried to disprove (overlay? loading? aging-color? link-primary?) and all alternatives fail. NOT the mobile overlay: SettingsView.tsx:464 `fixed inset-0 bg-black/50` is gated on `sidebarOpen && lg:hidden`; the screenshot is desktop (~1600px, static sidebar visible) so that overlay is not rendered. The actual root cause is hardcoded dark-mode-only Tailwind classes with NO light variant: SettingsSection.tsx:90,106 wrap the whole card in `bg-navy-800/50` (header/footer `bg-navy-900/50`) unconditionally — no `dark:` prefix — so the navy fill paints in light mode too. EmailDigestSettings.tsx compounds it: rows `bg-navy-900/30` (line 241), labels `text-white` (244), helper text `text-slate-500` (247), option cards `bg-navy-800/30` (204). Over the white SettingsView content area this navy block reads exactly as the reported 'dark scrim,' white headers invert, and dark-on-dark helper text disappears. So the finding's SYMPTOM is fully accurate; only its proposed mechanism (stuck loading/saving overlay, Honest-UI §4.1) is wrong — it is static theming, not an overlay, so the §4.1 'stuck overlay' framing should be dropped. Genuine violation of light-mode-readability §1/§9/§15 (WCAG AA contrast) and affects the whole SettingsSection panel family (Notifications/AI&Automation/Security), matching 'identical across panels.' Not aging-color, not link-primary, not a -ERR error screenshot, not a transient load (classes are static, persists after load). Severity corrected P0 -> P1: panels remain operable (toggles visible, selected cards show crimson borders, headers legible) so it is a severe broad light-mode theming/contrast break, not a functional/crash/data-loss blocker. Fix: add light-mode variants (e.g. bg-white/bg-slate-50 + dark:bg-navy-800/50, text-navy-900 dark:text-white, slate-600 helper) across SettingsSection.tsx and EmailDigestSettings.tsx and the rest of the SettingsSection-based panels.

The inputs render via shared SettingsInput (src/components/settings/shared/SettingsSection.tsx:214-225) which hardcodes `bg-navy-800 ... text-white border-white/10` with NO `dark:` variant — so it renders dark navy even in light mode. Not link=primary, not aging-color, not loading. Disproof of intentional-design: the settings shell (SettingsView.tsx) is correctly theme-aware (`bg-slate-50 dark:bg-navy-950`, `bg-white dark:bg-navy-900`), and sibling settings modules (NotificationsModule, ProfileModule) use the CORRECT theme-aware input pattern `bg-white dark:bg-white/5 text-slate-900 dark:text-white` — so a known-good pattern exists and the AI-settings family is the outlier. findings.verifyNote: Confirmed real defect at source level, not a false alarm. In src/components/AIChat/KimiWorkspace/ArtifactModuleHome.tsx line 199, the condition `(activeTab === 'recent' || activeTab === 'saved')` renders the SAME `<ArtifactsList artifacts={recentArtifacts} ...>` for both tabs. recentArtifacts comes from the single hook useModuleRecentArtifacts (line 85); there is no separate saved fetch, no filter, no per-tab scoping. The only difference between the two branches is the empty-state label (lines 206-213). This matches the screenshots: recent-light.png and saved-light.png are pixel-identical (same 6 rows: 'Stwórz: Tracker zadań...', 'Wypisz ryzyka...', 'Stwórz: Zestaw OKR...', 'Utw', 'Utw', 'Structured sheet draft'; same dates May 16/May 9 2026). findings.verifyNote: Verified against ground-truth code (src/components/AIChat/KimiWorkspace/ArtifactModuleHome.tsx line 590, ArtifactsList component). The 'ready' chip is rendered with: `text-xs font-medium text-slate-500 dark:text-slate-400 bg-slate-100 dark:bg-navy-800 px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full`. This confirms two hard violations of light-mode-readability §5 (badge MUST have bg + border + text 700/800): (1) NO border class at all, and (2) text is slate-500, well below the required 700/800. Screenshot corroborates — pale gray ghost pills barely separable from the off-white page bg. False-positive exemptions do NOT apply: it is not an aging-color (hardcoded slate, not rose/amber/emerald), not a link=primary crimson, not a loading/empty state (six populated rows render with the same persistent badge), and not an error-state capture. So it is a real, intentional-looking-but-incorrect styling defect, not a false alarm. However, I corrected severity P1->P2: this is a single low-prominence, uniform status pill (every row shows the same 'ready') carrying no action and no critical info; legibility is degraded but not blocking. The finding's prescriptive claim that 'ready' MUST become an emerald/success tone via statusChipTone is the reviewer's recommendation, not a hard canon requirement — a neutral chip tone is acceptable as long as it gets the mandated bg+border+text-700/800. The keep-worthy core is the readability/border violation, which fits the systemic badge-no-fill-in-light pattern and belongs in that sweep at P2, not as a standalone P1 blocker.
